outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score, did you pass with five? Subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Fifteen hard questions, score five and you pass. Ready? First one: which country has the most pyramids?
lines.a: Sudan! More than two hundred of them, about twice as many as Egypt. They were built by the kings of ancient Kush.

lines.q: Trick question. You're in a race and you pass the runner in second place. What place are you in now?
lines.a: Second! You took their place, you didn't pass the leader. Most people shout first.

lines.q: In which city was the Titanic built?
lines.a: Belfast! At the Harland and Wolff shipyard. It sailed from Southampton, which fools a lot of people. Building it took about three years.

lines.q: Which is the only planet named after a goddess?
lines.a: Venus! The Roman goddess of love. Every other planet is named after a male god. It's also the hottest planet, even hotter than Mercury.

lines.q: Nice start! Which gas makes up most of the air we breathe?
lines.a: Nitrogen! About seventy eight percent. Oxygen is only around twenty one percent. The last one percent is mostly argon.

lines.q: Round two: very hard. What was the tallest mountain in the world before Mount Everest was discovered?
lines.a: Mount Everest! It was already the tallest, people just hadn't measured it yet. Got you? Surveyors worked out its height in the eighteen fifties.

lines.q: Which is the only bird that can truly fly backwards?
lines.a: The hummingbird! Its wings can beat around fifty times a second, and it can even hover in place.

lines.q: Does England have a Fourth of July?
lines.a: Yes, every year! It just isn't a holiday there. Every country has a fourth of July, it comes right after the third. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: Still with me? What is the most common letter in English?
lines.a: E! It shows up in about one in every eight letters you read. T is a distant second. That's why it's worth just one point in Scrabble.

lines.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
lines.a: Three! Two pump blood to the gills, one to the rest of the body. And its blood is blue. It gets that color from copper.

lines.q: Final round: legend level. A plane crashes right on the border between the US and Canada. Where do they bury the survivors?
lines.a: Nowhere! Survivors are alive, you don't bury them. Did you start picking a country? Read it again, slowly.

lines.q: Which country sends London the giant Christmas tree in Trafalgar Square every year?
lines.a: Norway! Oslo has sent one every year since nineteen forty seven, as a thank you for British help in World War Two.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! A red house is made of red bricks. What is a greenhouse made of?
lines.a: Glass! Your brain wanted to say green bricks. That's why trick questions work.

lines.q: Which is the only number whose letters are in alphabetical order?
lines.a: Forty! F, O, R, T, Y. Check it yourself, no other number works.

lines.q: Final question. Which planet has the fastest winds in the solar system?
lines.a: Neptune! Winds up to about two thousand kilometres an hour. That's faster than the speed of sound on Earth. And it's the farthest planet from the Sun.
